raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, and the land feeds the family, so I do not make fancy plans. I do what has worked on my fields. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me. If one side is weak, the other can still bring something back. I cannot spend too much at once, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard, because if the crop turns yellow and thin, the harvest drops fast.

For wheat, I will sow in October like we always do here. I will use the seed I can buy nearby, the common kind everyone plants, not expensive special seed. Before sowing I will put base fertilizer, not too little, and then see the color of the wheat after winter. If it looks weak at jointing, I will add more urea. Water costs money from the well, but wheat usually needs a few irrigations here, so I will give water at the important times. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant maize right away. That gap is very short, so I will keep tillage simple and get the maize in quickly. Maize I also plant the usual local hybrid seed. I will put some fertilizer at planting, then a topdressing later if the stand looks good. If rain is short, I will pump well water once or twice, but not more unless the crop is clearly suffering. I mostly rely on family labor. On such a small piece of land, hiring people too much eats the income.
